body:
## Why
The board is one big DAG; a "track" is a connected subgraph, usually materialized by decompose (#11). Today the only execution engine is the dispatcher: global ready-frontier, one cold session per node — perfect durability, but tick latency and context re-derivation between dependent nodes. A track runner is a second engine: ONE session executes a whole subgraph like a workflow (nodes in dependency order, independent branches as subagents, context flowing in memory), while the board stays the source of truth.

## Design (agreed 2026-08-26)
- A track = a root task plus its descendants (or an explicit `kb.track` slug on each node). Same board, same issues — a track is a view, not a new object.
- The dispatcher, seeing a ready track root whose profile is `claude-track`, claims the ROOT lock and spawns one worker whose prompt is: "execute this subgraph — for each node: claim its lock (`hkb claim <n>`), do the work, finish it with its own terminal verb; run independent branches as subagents; stop at the frontier if a node blocks."
- Every node completion goes through the normal verbs → every node is a durable checkpoint. If the runner dies mid-track, the board still holds per-node truth and the ordinary dispatcher resumes node-by-node — no new crash semantics.
- Node locks claimed as-you-go (not all up front) so a dead runner never wedges the whole track.
- Concurrency caps count the track as ONE running slot (it is one session); per-node `kb.paths` guards still apply to protect against other concurrent workers.
- Out of scope: cross-harness tracks (a track whose nodes need different harnesses is simply not claimable as a track and falls back to node dispatch).

## What
- `src/track.js`: subgraph resolution (root → descendants via blocking edges), track-readiness (root ready AND all nodes on-board), and the runner prompt builder (reuses `workerContext` per node).
- Dispatcher: recognize track roots, claim + spawn the runner, and treat node-level verbs from inside the runner exactly like any worker's.
- Skill: a `## When you run a track` section teaching the claim→work→verb loop per node and subagent fan-out for independent branches.
- Tests against the fake-gh harness (#3): runner crash mid-track → dispatcher resumes remaining nodes; a blocking node parks only its branch.

## Done when
A 3-node chain executes end-to-end in one session with three result comments and three PRs (or one PR if the track declares a shared branch — decide and document), and killing the runner after node 1 leaves a board the plain dispatcher finishes correctly.
title: Track runner: execute a claimed subgraph workflow-style, checkpointing every node through the board
